followed.title: Voter Information Service - Options to vote
followed.text_sample: Voter Information Service - Options to vote Skip to main content Home Français Voter Information Service Menu Start new search FAQ Map Candidates Returning officer Profile Past results Options to vote Scarborough North (Ontario) Vote now Vote in person You can vote in person at your Elections Canada office, any time before 6:00 p.m. (local time) on December 1. Go to your local Elections Canada office. Vote by mail You can vote by mail if you apply by December 1, 6 p.m. (Eastern time). Fill out the form here. Vote at advance polls Click on 'Where do I vote?' to get advanced polling dates and hours. Additional advance polling locations may be available in some remote communities, and voting hours may vary. The address of your assigned polling place will be on the voter information card that you will receive in the mail. You can also find the address here after November 10. Vote on election day You can vote at your assigned polling place on Monday, December 7, 2026. The address of your assigned polling place will be on the voter information card that you will receive in the mail. You can also find the address here after November 10. Provincial Voting Places.notes:
A voting place is the building or facility where voters of one or more voting areas are assigned to vote.
(Election Act, s. 1, 81)

This dataset contains spatial points representative of voting opportunities for use in provincial electoral events.  

Each voting place is identified by a three character electoral district code (e.g. CHC is an abbreviation of the Chilliwack electoral district).  A voting place is identified by a standard address ID, street address, locality and building name.

A voting place is classified by type based on its use in an electoral event; Advance - for use in advance voting opportunities, General - for use on general voting day, and Advance and General which are used for throughout the voting period of electoral event.

The status of a voting place is indicative of whether a voting place is proposed or has been confirmed for an electoral event.  The event name and event date fields indicates which electoral event a voting place is used for.

This dataset includes voting places for the 2017 Provincial General Election, the 2018 West-Kelowna By-election, the 2019 Nanaimo By-election, the 2020 Provincial General Election, the 2022 Surrey South By-election, the 2023 Langford-Juan de Fuca By-election, the 2023 Vancouver-Mount Pleasant By-election, the 2024 Provincial General Election and the 2026 Provincial General Election.

Provincial Voting Areas to Voting Place.notes:
This table provides the assignment of voting areas (VAs) to a general voting place for provincial electoral events.

Each voting area is shown with the three character electoral district code followed by the numeric voting area code (e.g. CHC009 is voting area 009 in the Chilliwack electoral district).  The assigned voting place is identified by a standard address ID, street address, locality and building name.  

The currency date is indicative of when the data was extracted.  The event name and event date fields indicates which electoral event a voting area was assigned to a particular voting place.

This dataset includes voting area to voting place assignments for the 2017 Provincial General Election, the 2018 West-Kelowna By-election, the 2019 Nanaimo By-election, the 2020 Provincial General Election, the 2022 Surrey South By-election, the 2023 Langford-Juan de Fuca By-election, the 2023 Vancouver-Mount Pleasant By-election, the 2024 Provincial General Election and the 2026 Provincial General Election.
